elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.1: "Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's behalf a licence to use the Services"; the prior exclusion "Customer alone ... without Affiliates or contractors" is deleted. "Customer" is defined as Meridian Fieldworks, Inc. alone, so the express Affiliate grant is additive, not duplicative (13.2 covers only paid-up software/Vendor Technology, a different licence scope).

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.1 grants to "contractors acting on Customer's behalf"; 13.2 separately permits contractors to support paid-up material. No retained language contradicts the new grant.
Retained 13.2: "delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis ... Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence".

Retained 13.2 grants an "irrevocable" paid-up licence; retained 13.3 limits revocation/suspension to a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and cure, and the at-will revocation formerly in 13.1 is removed.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.1 (the Services/subscription licence): "terminable only for Customer's uncured material breach", replacing "revocable at Vendor's sole discretion"; consistent with 13.3's notice-and-cure limit.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Retained 13.3: "Customer may transfer its licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24." The conflicting word "non-transferable" in 13.1 was deleted, so the Services licence is now within that transfer right. The right is conditioned on Section 24's permitted-assignment scope, which is a live internal cross-reference rather than an undefined trigger.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.1 covers "its Affiliates" unconditionally, which exceeds (and therefore satisfies) coverage on written notice; 13.2 already covered Affiliates for paid-up material.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Retained 13.3 permits transfer of licence rights to "an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24"; the deletion of "non-transferable" from 13.1 removes the contradiction.

reasons: Original 13.1 was walk-away (Customer alone, affiliates and contractors expressly excluded, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion), so a redline was warranted; the finding status "deviation" is correct.

The single edit to 13.1 reaches the full preferred level: affiliates and contractors are added, at-will revocation is replaced with termination only for uncured material breach, and the perpetual/irrevocable paid-up grant (13.2) and successor transfer right (13.3) are retained unchanged.

Minimality holds: only the words creating the failures were touched. Deletion of "non-transferable" is necessary, not cosmetic, because it directly contradicts the retained 13.3 transfer right that carries the successor element; no survival tails, procedures, or extraneous obligations were added.

No duplicate coverage: "Customer" is defined as Meridian Fieldworks, Inc. alone and does not include Affiliates, and 13.2's Affiliate grant is limited to paid-up software/Vendor Technology, a different licence than the 13.1 Services licence. No separate personnel/access edit was added, correctly.
Intent preserved: 13.1's new breach-based termination standard is compatible with 13.3's notice-and-cure revocation limit; no dangling cross-references or undefined terms are introduced.

Residual point for the drafter (not a failure): the successor transfer in 13.3 remains gated on "an assignment permitted by Section 24". If Section 24 does not permit assignment to an M&A successor without Vendor consent, the transferability element would become conditional and should be shored up under the ASSIGN rule rather than by further editing Section 13.
